extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimentalists, and scholars reforming scientific method
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reconstructing natural philosophy: how to collect and organize experiments, devise a new inductive method, build axioms from particulars, and reform scientific labor and institutions. Emphasizes compilation of natural history, new forms of induction, and practical organization (tables, writing, division of labor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance experiment and reason (bee model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who have treated of the sciences have been either empirics or dogmatical... The true labor of philosophy resembles [the bee], for it neither relies entirely or principally on the powers of the mind, nor yet lays up in the memory the matter afforded by the experiments of natural history and mechanics in its raw state, but changes and works it in the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the two extremes: pure empiricism (merely collecting facts) and pure dogmatism (spinning webs of theory). Good natural philosophy must extract material from experience and process it with reason—working and fashioning particulars into informed understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek pure, unmixed natural philosophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural philosophy is not yet to be found unadulterated, but is impure and corrupted--by logic in the school of Aristotle, by natural theology in that of Plato, by mathematics in the second school of Plato... which ought rather to terminate natural philosophy than to generate or create it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue a form of natural philosophy free from dominating, foreign disciplines or sectarian dogma; avoid letting auxiliary arts (formal logic, theology, abstruse mathematics) dictate natural-philosophical conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abolish common theories and reapply mind to particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: No one has yet been found possessed of sufficient firmness and severity to resolve upon and undertake the task of entirely abolishing common theories and notions, and applying the mind afresh, when thus cleared and levelled, to particular researches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporarily suspend received doctrines and preconceived generalities; approach particulars anew and let fresh inquiry build the resulting axioms rather than force particulars to fit old theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build philosophy on a firm foundation of experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundations of experience (our sole resource) have hitherto failed completely or have been very weak; nor has a store and collection of particular facts, capable of informing the mind or in any way satisfactory, been either sought after or amassed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amass a well-ascertained, purpose-built natural history (not mere species-lists) that serves directly as the basis for deriving causal axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect 'enlightening' experiments (not only profitable ones)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a very great scarcity of those which best inform and assist the understanding... these experiments we have termed enlightening, to distinguish them from those which are profitable. They possess this wonderful property... they never deceive or fail you; for being used only to discover the natural cause of some object, whatever be the result, they equally satisfy your aim by deciding the question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize experiments designed to reveal causes and test hypotheses (even if they lack immediate practical utility) over merely commercially useful trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt a determined, regular method and order for experience
rubrics_metrics.description: We must not only search for, and procure a greater number of experiments, but also introduce a completely different method, order, and progress of continuing and promoting experience. For vague and arbitrary experience is... mere groping in the dark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize experimental work according to explicit rules and sequences rather than ad hoc or intermittent effort; promote continuity and systematic progression in empirical investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit experiments and observations to writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Meditation has hitherto done more for discovery than writing, and no experiments have been committed to paper. We cannot, however, approve of any mode of discovery without writing...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record experiments, observations, and raw particulars in durable written form to enable verification, synthesis, and cumulative progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize particulars into living tables of discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: We must put its forces in due order and array, by means of proper and well arranged, and, as it were, living tables of discovery of these matters, which are the subject of investigation, and the mind then apply itself to the ready prepared and digested aid which such tables afford.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create structured, updatable tables/indexes of facts and experiments to make particulars accessible and to guide reasoning and further experimentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascend from particulars to axioms and descend to effects
rubrics_metrics.description: The more important [results] are to be derived from the new light of axioms, deduced by certain method and rule from the above particulars, and pointing out and defining new particulars in their turn. Our road... rises and falls, ascending to axioms, and descending to effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not stop at collecting particulars—use them to infer intermediate and general axioms, then use those axioms to predict and test new effects (a cyclical ascent and descent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid leaping from particulars to remote general axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: Nor can we suffer the understanding to jump and fly from particulars to remote and most general axioms... the assent shall proceed by a true scale and successive steps, without interruption or breach, from particulars to the lesser axioms, thence to the intermediate, and lastly, to the most general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require successive, verifiable inferential steps (building intermediate axioms) rather than immediate acceptance of sweeping general principles from limited data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and rely on intermediate axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: The intermediate are true, solid, full of life, and upon them depend the business and fortune of mankind; beyond these are the really general, but not abstract, axioms, which are truly limited by the intermediate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on establishing mid-level, practically significant axioms that bridge experiment and high-level theory; these are the most valuable for application and further discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invent a new form of induction using exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: The induction which proceeds by simple enumeration is puerile... should separate nature by proper rejections and exclusions, and then conclude for the affirmative, after collecting a sufficient number of negatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace naive enumeration with an inductive method that systematically eliminates alternatives (collecting negative instances) so that affirmative conclusions rest on robust exclusions and sufficient negative evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use induction to define notions as well as discover axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: The assistance of induction is to serve us not only in the discovery of axioms, but also in defining our notions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply inductive procedures to clarify and refine concepts/definitions, not only to infer causal laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test axioms for generality by whether they point to new particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: We must examine and try whether the axiom we derive be only fitted and calculated for the particular instances from which it is deduced, or whether it be more extensive and general... whether it confirm its own extent and generality by giving surety, as it were, in pointing out new particulars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate a proposed axiom by its ability to predict or suggest novel phenomena—axioms should be self-confirming by leading to correct anticipation of new particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unify sciences to prevent schism and aid progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The extending of natural philosophy and reducing particular sciences to that one, so as to prevent any schism or dismembering of the sciences; without which we cannot hope to advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to integrate specialized subjects under a coherent natural philosophy to avoid fragmentation that impedes cumulative understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer regular investigation over chance discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: If many useful discoveries have occurred to mankind by chance... it must necessarily be acknowledged that much more may be brought to light by investigation and attention, if it be regular and orderly, not hasty and interrupted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design research programs that are systematic rather than relying on serendipity; regular attention and methodical work will outpace chance discoveries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer, compare, and apply experiments (literate experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transferring the experiments from one art to another... (when all the experiments of each have been collected and arranged...) many new experiments may be discovered... by what we term literate experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-apply experimentally proven operations across domains and disciplines (documenting and comparing results) to reveal novel effects and useful innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate substantial labor and resources to compiling natural history
rubrics_metrics.description: Their infinite expenditure of talent, time, and fortune, in matters and studies of far inferior importance... a small portion of which applied to sound and solid learning would be sufficient to overcome every difficulty... such a collection of natural and experimental history... is a great and as it were royal work, requiring much labor and expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit institutional time, money, and organized effort to the large-scale compilation of experiments and observations—the task is costly but foundational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not fear the multitude of particulars; embrace them
rubrics_metrics.description: Let no one be alarmed at the multitude of particulars, but rather inclined to hope on that very account... particular phenomena of the arts and nature are in reality but as a handful, when compared with the fictions of the imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the abundance of observed particulars as an asset for grounding reliable axioms; avoid premature abstraction that discards empirical detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote division of labor and cumulative collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Men will then only begin to know their own power, when each performs a separate part, instead of undertaking in crowds the same work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize collaborative, distributed tasks for collecting and testing particulars (specialization and coordinated effort across practitioners and generations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept and correct early experimental errors
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be some... who... will meet with some uncertainty, or perhaps fallacy, in the experiments themselves... it must needs happen in beginnings... many experiments in natural history may be erroneously believed and admitted, which are easily expunged and rejected afterward, by the discovery of causes and axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and tolerate initial inaccuracies in empirical compilations; treat them as corrigible as the inductive program refines causes and axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include common, mean, and seemingly lowly particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: The mean and splendid alike exist... the mean and sordid instances... valuable light and information emanate from mean and sordid instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exclude ordinary, unglamorous, or 'filthy' observations from natural history—such particulars can yield crucial causal insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize experiments that 'afford light' over immediate profit
rubrics_metrics.description: We look for experiments that shall afford light rather than profit, imitating the divine creation... For, in fact, the knowledge of simple natures, when sufficiently investigated and defined, resembles light...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value experiments that clarify fundamental natures and generate conceptual illumination even if they have no direct practical payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not found sects or promise particular effects; seek causes and axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: We bestow not our labor on such theoretical and, at the same time, useless topics... we neither offer nor promise particular effects... our course and method... is such as not to deduce effects from effects, nor experiments from experiments... but... to deduce causes and axioms from effects and experiments; and new effects and experiments from those causes and axioms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid creating dogmatic schools or making speculative promises of immediate inventions; focus on deriving causal axioms from experiments and then using those axioms to generate reliable new effects.
